question: The forthcoming Circular Economy Act presents an opportunity to strengthen the single market for circular materials and improve the EU’s resource resilience. Stakeholders continue to identify regulatory barriers to the recognition of secondary raw materials across the EU, creating legal uncertainty for companies operating across borders. For instance, inconsistent approaches to waste classification and end-of-waste criteria prevent recovered materials from circulating freely between Member States. Given this: 1.

Will the Commission introduce harmonised end-of-waste criteria and mutual recognition mechanisms to ensure that secondary raw materials in one Member State can circulate freely across the single market?
Will it simplify waste shipment and permitting rules for recyclable materials to facilitate the development of cross-border recycling capacity and circularity hubs within the EU?
